framing: Causes proposed in open-access papers, each quoted exactly with its location. They are hypotheses for an engineer to check against this fab's own process history, not diagnoses: the papers state them briefly, often by citing older work, and none was established on this data. No open-access source read for this table states a cause for the Loc or Near-full patterns.

causes.label: Center
causes.hypothesis: Associated in the literature with thin-film deposition, plasma or etching problems.

quotes.quote: Scratch is caused by machine handling, while Center and Edge-Ring are caused by thin film deposition and etching problems
For example, the center type has the effect of problems in the plasma area or thin-film deposition,
quotes.location: Results and discussion, Experiment, Data description (citing Hansen and Thyregod 1998, ref. 28)

causes.label: Center
causes.hypothesis: Associated with uneven mechanical polishing or abnormal liquid pressure.

quotes.quote: For example, the Center pattern means that the mechanical polishing is uneven, or the pressure of the liquid is abnormal.

causes.label: Center
causes.hypothesis: A circular, center-located pattern is associated with chemical stains or mechanical equipment faults.

quotes.quote: often corresponds to chemical stains or mechanical equipment faults

causes.label: Donut
causes.hypothesis: A center-located donut pattern is associated with possible tooling problems.

quotes.quote: is routinely observed in wafer data due to possible tooling problems

causes.label: Edge-Loc
causes.hypothesis: Associated with uneven heating during the diffusion process.

quotes.quote: and the edge-loc type has the same effect as uneven heating during the diffusion process.
quotes.location: Results and discussion, Experiment, Data description (citing Hansen and Thyregod 1998, ref. 28)

causes.label: Edge-Loc
causes.hypothesis: A zone-shaped, edge-located pattern is associated with uneven polishing or edge-die effects (the source describes an edge zone, which corresponds most closely to Edge-Loc).

quotes.quote: can be traced to uneven polishing or edge-die effects

causes.label: Edge-Ring
causes.hypothesis: Associated in the literature with etching or thin-film deposition problems.

quotes.quote: Scratch is caused by machine handling, while Center and Edge-Ring are caused by thin film deposition and etching problems

causes.label: Edge-Ring
causes.hypothesis: Associated with abnormal temperature control during annealing.

quotes.quote: Abnormal temperature control during annealing may lead to an Edge-Ring pattern.

causes.label: Scratch
causes.hypothesis: Associated with wafer handling, moving or cutting.

quotes.quote: Scratch is caused by machine handling, while Center and Edge-Ring are caused by thin film deposition and etching problems
The Scratch pattern indicates an exception in the moving or cutting processes.

causes.label: Random
causes.hypothesis: Randomly scattered failing dies are associated with ordinary process variation or a poorly controlled process environment rather than with one assignable source.

quotes.quote: since they are merely artifacts of random process variation
is often due to a lack of process environment management or factors that are difficult to control directly.
quotes.location: 3.2 Random Noise Filtering and Data Augmentation (about random noise, not the Random class)
